description: We are a multidisciplinary team of four from Saudi Arabia, combining Data Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Science, and Computer & Network Engineering.
summary: Martian Map helps an astronaut walk on Mars without getting lost. We built an interactive web map of one walking route in Jezero Crater, from the Perseverance landing site to the Western Delta Deposit and the Western Breach. Instead of searching through many separate NASA tools, the astronaut sees everything in one place: the path, the stops along the way, the geology, and where the ground gets steep. Each stop explains why it matters, whether it is a science target or a hazard, so the astronaut can follow the route safely.
details:
Martian Map is a focused route planner for a Marswalk in Jezero Crater, built to work like a GPS for an astronaut.

The problem

NASA's data about Jezero already exists, but it is spread across many layers, points and tools. Mars Trek covers the whole planet, so planning one walk means opening many points, measuring distances and reading elevation by hand, and it is easy to get lost in a map that large.

What it does

Our map brings that data together for one route only. The astronaut sees the path, the slopes and the troughs around it, and can turn each layer on or off: high-resolution imagery, geology and structures. Every stop explains why the astronaut stops there, either a science target or a hazard. An elevation profile shows where the walk gets steep.

Why this route

The route starts at the Perseverance landing ellipse and reaches the Western Delta Deposit and the Western Breach. We measured each leg in Mars Trek and checked it against NASA's EVA range limits, so the route stays within a safe distance while still covering varied terrain and information. The steepest section, a climb of about 53 m at the delta front found in MOLA elevation data, is marked as a hazard.

How it works

- Python (geopandas, shapely) clips the USGS geologic map to the Jezero area and builds the route file (GeoJSON) from our selected stops.

- Elevation profiles are exported from Mars Trek (MOLA) as CSV.

- A web page built with HTML, JavaScript, Leaflet and Chart.js displays the layers, stops and elevation chart, hosted on GitHub Pages.

Future work

- Faster loading when zooming in and out.

- Awareness beyond the work area, so the astronaut knows the conditions and possible problems around them, not only along the route.

- A practical, clear 3D view of the terrain.

- Guidance for emergencies or unexpected events during the walk.

- A cleaner interface with less clutter, so key information is clear at a glance.

- Data analysis and prediction to support decisions on the route.

Source code: https://github.com/m000n-o00o/martian-map
